method: Re-established the official year totals and ordered field choices from the dated OER and re-read the dated Ocasys network, labour, research and statistics content. Checked underlying UCR workbook evidence before reviewing the frozen schedules, comparison rows, audience references and descriptions.
findings: The first year is 60 EC. The second year combines 45 EC required work with Social Networks and its corresponding project for 15 EC. The third year combines 25 EC required work, a different 5 EC field course and a 30 EC broadening minor. The first listed different field is Labour Sociology. The neighbourhood project needs two first-year statistics passes. Thesis entry requires all first-year units and all projects.

The three UCR directions sustain broad sociological inquiry, work and organisations, and crime and public safety. All retain five dedicated sociology courses. The employment option focuses on organisational and economic evidence. The safety option uses justice institutions, youth resilience and collective action, without claiming forensic or digital crime study. The pairwise differences are 60, 60 and 75 EC in each direction. The corrected terms and substitution pass.

The dated statistics courses and workbook distinguish regression, variance and categorical models, applied econometrics and basic data cleaning. HCBPSYC211 has substantive overlap with the third statistics course, while introductory Data Science does not. Introductory sociology includes classical thought but does not replace the separate classical-text course. Social influence is different from network analysis, and leadership psychology does not replace Labour Sociology.

The normal comparison shows three evidenced concepts, both selected notes and all verified field and progression references. The 31 component titles and the 38 selected UCR descriptions agree with the reviewed records. Optional independent research sits alongside the thesis outside scheduled credits.
